text.p: The Atlanta Braves fought off elimination with a vengence Monday, clobbering the St Louis Cardinals 14-0 on Monday to cut the Cards' lead to 3-2 in the best-of-seven-games National League Championship Series.
Chipper Jones and Jeff Blauser drove in two runs each in a five-run first inning and John Smoltz won his third post-season game.
The defending World Series champion Braves wasted no time serving notice they will not go quietly. It took them four batters to score three runs and two innings to open a 7-0 lead.
Although the Cardinals still lead the series, they must win in Atlanta to face the New York Yankees in the World Series, which begin Saturday.
The Braves have won eight of their last nine post-season games at home.

St. Louis is the only team in major-league history to twice blow a 3-1 lead in the post-season. The Cardinals did it in the 1968 World Series against Detroit and the 1985 World Series against Kansas City. No National League team has ever rallied from a 3-1 deficit in the NLCS.

Jones had two hits and three RBI, Marquis Grissom had three hits and scored twice, and Javy Lopez and Mark Lemke both tied the NLCS record with four hits. Lopez homered and scored four runs and Fred McGriff hit his seventh career post-season homer.
The Braves rapped out 22 hits, smashing the NLCS mark of 16 set by the Chicago Cubs in 1984 and breaking the all-time LCS record of 19 set by the Yankees in 1981.

Smoltz, who won his 27th game this year, joined the hitting spree, going 2-for-4 with an RBI and a run scored. The right-hander breezed through seven scoreless innings, allowing seven hits and a walk while striking out seven. He improved to 8-1 all-time in the post-season.

St. Louis rallied from a three-run deficit to win Game Four and was poised for the clincher with Todd Stottlemyre, who had won both of his post-season starts. But it took just 13 pitches to dampen hopes of a pennant celebration.

Grissom singled and Mark Lemke doubled. Jones doubled for two runs and scored on McGriff's bloop single. Ryan Klesko struck out and Lopez's grounder was mishandled by third baseman Gary Gaetti, who only got a force play.
That proved costly when Jermaine Dye singled and Blauser sent a triple to the gap in right-centre, scoring two more. Smoltz grounded out to end the inning, then took the mound with a 5-0 lead.
The National League Cy Young Award favourite nearly gave some of it back, allowing three consecutive two-out singles to load the bases. But Grissom tracked down John Mabry's liner in centre.

The Braves responded with two more runs, chasing Stottlemyre. Grissom, Lemke and Jones each singled to make it 6-0 and Danny Jackson came on and got McGriff to line into a double play. But Klesko singled home another run.
